qualitative.gate_2_reason: Discretionary and deferrable travel/hospitality service; highly cyclical lodging spend easily forgone or traded down in economic downturns.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 2 (REJECT). Hotel lodging and hospitality represent discretionary, deferrable travel expenditures highly sensitive to global economic cycles, corporate travel budgets, and consumer leisure spending. Despite shifting to an asset-light management and franchise model across ~5,600 hotels, hotel room nights are easily forgone or traded down during downturns, failing Munger's non-deferrable essential need standard.
qualitative.evidence: Accor SA is a French multinational hospitality franchisor and manager operating over 5,600 hotels across 110+ countries under 45+ brands (including Ibis, Novotel, Mercure, Sofitel, Pullman, and Fairmont). While its asset-light transition (divesting owned real estate via AccorInvest) has reduced maintenance capex intensity, group earnings and RevPAR remain deeply cyclical and tethered to discretionary travel demand. During the pandemic, group revenues dropped by over 50% and operating earnings swung to severe losses. Even post-recovery, historical ROIC has hovered between 5% and 8%, failing to reliably clear the 12% capital efficiency hurdle. Furthermore, Accor faces severe distribution pressure from online travel agency gatekeepers (Booking Holdings, Expedia) and alternative accommodation platforms (Airbnb), diluting brand pricing power.
